what: Where the example output distributed with the published base model comes from, and which input rate produced it. Recorded by hand on 2026-10-10 from the published repository and from the copy on the server; the numbers that can be recomputed are in engine_validation_200hz.json.

server_copy.distributed_outputs: results/example/sugarR.parquet and sugarR_100Hz.parquet; data/shiu2024/example/ holds identical copies (md5 6ead3256ec84df79d077c7c7c73dc8db and bbfe8de603474a9fe5f2feab5cdcf146)

released_model_py.line: 'r_poi'     : 150*Hz,                 # default rate of the Poisson inputs

history.message: removed large data files from repo
Fixed minor typos and comments in model.py

released_model_py.note: model.py has two commits; the rate line is 150*Hz in both, so no committed version of the code has a 200-Hz default.

example_notebook.statement_in_current_version: By default, the neurons are excited at 200 Hz.

commit_that_introduced_the_statement.message: Update example to state default is 200 Hz.ipynb
commit_that_introduced_the_statement.added_line: In the previous experiment, sugar neurons were activated by default at 200 Hz. We want to change the stimulation frequency.

notebook_with_stored_outputs.note: The notebook committed with the distributed output shows that output (511,566 spikes, stimulated neurons near 200 Hz) as the result of the call without a rate argument, while model.py of the same commit sets 150 Hz. The output was therefore produced with a default of 200 Hz that is not in any committed model.py. The later versions of the notebook have no stored outputs.

sources: server: ext/Drosophila_brain_model/model.py, example.ipynb, environment.yml, environment_full.yml; results/example/*.parquet read with pandas
